title: OK Serving Bowl for COLD Foods
text:
OK Serving Bowl for COLD Foods. If you are shopping for dishes for the first time in a while you’ll notice a plethora of dishes made of Melamine. The prices are reasonable and the design choices plentiful. As a potter who understands the dangers dishes can pose due to the glazes used, I decided to dig into what Melamine is and whether I wanted to use it with my family.

So let’s start with what exactly is Melamine?

Melamine is an organic compound also called urea or carbamide, that is mixed with formaldehyde to form a polymer resin. Melamine can also be mixed with other inorganic compounds to become a flame retardant, a fertilizer and a plasticizer for concrete.

Melamine is commonly used to make strong hard plastic dinnerware but is made using formaldehyde and the safety of melamine dishes is controversial.

Any heat can cause these chemicals and resins to migrate into your food, so it’s wise to stay away from plastic and melamine tableware options as they aren’t exactly the safest dishes to use for health.

Melamine plates are not oven safe and the FDA advises against using melamine in microwave ovens. Melamine is made from melamine-formaldehyde resin, and the melamine can contaminate food at 160°F and above.

Pfaltzgraff?

I decided to do a bit more digging... Like many, I have been eating off Pfaltzgraff dishes my entire life. I have the dishes my mom had that I then inherited - they are Pfaltzgraff dishes that have been in daily use for 45+ years.

Pfaltzgraff had been produced in Pennsylvania since 1811 with the first factory opening in 1865. Pfaltzgraff was truly an American standard that many of us knew, grew up with and the name carries weight.

In 2005 the Pfaltzgraff Co. was sold to Lifetime Brands, Inc. It was at this time the vast majority of production moved from the US to Mexico and China. After doing quite a bit of digging, from what I can decipher, of course this information is not easily found, it appears the Melamine lines are produced in China.

So My Thoughts on this Melamine Serving Bowl...

There is no question that it’s plastic. This will be a personal preference to some degree but I think plastic serving dishes look cheap. Yeah the outside looks like marble - kind of. It is lightweight and Melamine is harder to break than ceramic - though it will break, especially if it’s cold.

After extensively researching Melamine dish safety I’m not comfortable with the potential risk of chemical leaching when temperatures are over 160°F or if foods are acidic. These dishes are definitely not microwave or oven safe. Something I always have to keep in mind is that while I would know not to microwave anything within this bowl that doesn’t mean my son or a guest would know that.

This bowl is one that I store in a different cabinet and use when we are going to a pot luck and I want to take banana pudding or the like. It works ok for that, it washes well and looks nice. Beyond that type of use I would not recommend it.
